title: The teaching failed, not the learner
statement: Judge stand-alone instruction by whether a newcomer could answer most of its check questions after one pass; if they could not, the instruction failed, not the learner.
example: The bar is at least 2 of 3 check questions answered after watching once.
detail: The video-script check starts from the premise that a short video is the only teacher and no one can step in, so a student who can't answer the check questions after watching means the video failed (`shadow-bench/src/inceptbench/prompts/video_script/evaluation.txt`). Before scoring, the judge imagines a student new to the topic and asks whether, after one viewing, they could answer at least 2 of 3 multiple-choice questions on the stated idea; if not, the ideas chosen, their number or the explanation is at fault.
against: The newcomer is imagined by the judge, not observed: 'Imagine a student who has never seen this topic before.' (`shadow-bench/src/inceptbench/prompts/video_script/evaluation.txt`, line 30). No student data feeds the check.

evidence.quote: **The video IS the teacher — no instructor rescue is possible.** If a student watches a video and cannot answer the CFU items after watching, the video failed — not the student.
Imagine a student who has never seen this topic before. After watching this video once, can they answer ≥2 out of 3 MCQs on the stated KC?
someone unfamiliar with the topic can use the taught information to answer the aligned checks.
